newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African hospital firm NetCare to list on JSE.
newsitem.headline: S.African hospital firm NetCare to list on JSE.

text.p: Newly-formed specialist hospital management company Network Healthcare Holdings Ltd (NetCare) announced late Wednesday that it would be listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on December 4.

NetCare combines the businesses of former specialist medical corporation Clin-Run as well as several of Clin-Run's managed hospitals and clinics and expects an initial market capitalisation of 286 million rand, it said.

"This is a unique accomplishment because of the fiercely competitive industry it is entering into which has been substantially controlled by large commercial institutions and protected by high costs of entry," NetCare non-executive director Michael Sacks said at the launch of the listing.
NetCare said in a statement that several large institutions had already subscribed for shares in the group, including Fedsure, MLS Bank and Northern Medical Society.
"We have a number of strategic partners and they bring, not only their cash resources, but also their expertise," said NetCare managing director and founder Jack Shevel.
He added that six other institutions had shown interest.
Netcare said that by listing it hoped to offset its debts and expand into South Africa's rapidly changing managed healthcare industry.
"Managed care is already becoming established in South Africa, and doctors as well as specialists have learned that it is rooted in economics," Shevel said.
The country's healthcare industry has recently seen the private sector increasingly take up the challenge of providing efficient and affordable healthcare.
Shevel added that after the listing, Netcare's hospitals will have more than 600 beds and an estimated turnover for the year to August 1997 of 172 million rand.
It would also have more than 40 million rand in cash in hand, no debt and an estimated after-tax profit of more than 23.6 million rand, Shevel said.
He said the NetCare group was developed over seven years by assembling a network of medical colleagues who invested in and practised at hospitals and clinics within the group.
Shevel and the 300-strong network of medical professionals involved will convert their interests in the group into NetCare shares at 100 cents each.

NetCare's hospitals and clinics include: Sunninghill Hospital in Sandton, Pretoria's Femina Clinic, Johannesburg city's Bagleystone Clinic, Ferncrest Hospital in Rustenburg, the Vaalpark Hospital in Sasolburg, as well as the new Umhlanga Hospital in KwaZulu-Natal.
